subject: Purchase route & security gating — next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Stanton <alex@novacorp.com>, Procurement Ops <procure@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Purchase route & security gating — next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can converge on the procurement path: 

What we covered
- Core ask: production inference for customer-facing chat (low-latency, dedicated pool).
- Expected usage: ~250k tokens/month steady-state; occasional spikes during campaigns.
- Security gating: SOC 2 report + DPA required by your security team; procurement flagged vendor-scoped questionnaire (looks like a standard 60-question).

Decision points we need to confirm
1) Preferred payment mechanism: purchase order (PO) vs. corporate card vs. cloud marketplace listing (AWS Marketplace).
2) Timing for SOC 2/DPA review and whether procurement will accept our standard DPA or request changes.
3) Who will own the security questionnaire: your security lead or procurement? If you prefer we can complete the vendor side and loop your reviewer.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
- I attached our SOC 2 summary and DPA template for their review.
- If PO: we can send a standard order form + SOW and support redlines.
- If Marketplace: we can provide AMI/Subscription guidance but note entitlements and billing cadence differ.

Can you confirm 1) which payment route you prefer, and 2) the contact for the security questionnaire? Once I have those I’ll put together a short mutual action plan and timeline.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with procurement if that helps.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2026.pdf, Redwood_DPA_Template.docx

From: Alex Stanton <alex@novacorp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procure@novacorp.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Purchase route & security gating — next steps

Thanks Aditya — great demo. A few quick answers from our side: 

- Payment preference: procurement prefers a PO and standard Net30 invoice flow. Marketplace would be acceptable only if the pricing cadence and commitments match our internal forecasting; it tends to be easier for projects that need fast onboarding, but PO is our default.
- SOC 2/DPA: our security team needs the SOC 2 Type II report and the DPA; we will review your standard DPA and flag any clauses we need changed.
- Questionnaire: procurement has asked that our security team (Jenna Li, cc’d on procure@novacorp.com) fills out the vendor questionnaire, but they expect the vendor to pre-populate technical answers where appropriate. I’ll loop Jenna into the next message.

Would be helpful to get a short mutual action plan with dates — procurement is aiming to have vendor in place by end of May.

—Alex
Alex Stanton
Head of Product, NovaCorp
alex@novacorp.com

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Purchase route & security gating — next steps

Alex — great, thanks for the clarity. I’ve attached the SOC 2 summary (full report link in the footer) and our standard DPA template. I also started a short mutual action plan (attached spreadsheet) with target dates so procurement can see the milestones. Highlights below: 

Mutual action plan (high level)
- Week 1 (Apr 19–25): Security team reviews SOC 2 & DPA; vendor pre-populates questionnaire.
- Week 2 (Apr 26–May 2): Procurement issues PO terms; we receive signed PO and countersign order form.
- Week 3 (May 3–9): Provision Dedicated pool and run smoke tests; knowledge transfer session.

Notes on marketplace vs PO
- PO path: straightforward for your finance team, supports Net30 and custom invoicing, and avoids marketplace fees. Lead time for provisioning is the same.
- Marketplace path: simplifies legal (consumption agreement via marketplace) but may add billing cadence constraints and platform fees; good if you want a faster sandbox experience without PO sign-off.

Questionnaire support
- We’ll pre-fill the technical and architecture sections (data flows, encryption, access controls). If Jenna prefers, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough to walk through any flagged answers.

Action items
- Alex / Jenna: confirm questionnaire owner and preferred PO contact.
- Marissa / Ben (cc’d): we may need expedited legal review if they push significant DPA redlines — please flag availability next week for a short review.

Links/attachments included: SOC2 report summary + link, DPA template, Mutual_Action_Plan_NovaCorp.xlsx, HubSpot record HS-REC-4592, DocuSign envelope prep link.

If that timeline looks good I’ll send the order form and the pre-filled questionnaire by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan_NovaCorp.xlsx, Redwood_SOC2_Report_2026.pdf, Redwood_DPA_Template.docx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: NovaCorp — procurement lane and potential legal review (quick sync)

Marissa / Ben — quick internal note following the exchange with NovaCorp. Key points: 

- They prefer PO / Net30; marketplace is a secondary option if legal/billing complexity becomes a blocker.
- Security: need SOC 2 Type II (we provided report link) and DPA review. Procurement expects vendor to pre-populate questionnaire; Jenna from their security team will own final sign-off.
- Timeline request: customer wants vendor selected by end of May (roughly 6 weeks).

Asks for you both:
- Marissa: can you confirm legal bandwidth next week to field any DPA redlines? If they push changes to data residency or audit clauses we’ll likely need a quick exception review.
- Ben: please prepare an order form (standard Redwood order form) and one-page SOW showing the dedicated pool sizing and expected costs for PO finance review.

I’ll prepare the pre-filled questionnaire draft and the order form templates; will share both with you before sending to procurement.

Thanks — aim to be proactive so we keep the May timeline intact.

—Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
